head_commit.message:
feat: page-bounded aggregator fetch loop with amount-derived search budget (#896)

* feat: page the aggregator by requested amount

Adzuna and JSearch previously issued exactly one request per search
regardless of how many jobs the user asked for, so any amount above one
page silently under-filled.

Adzuna now loops `page in 1..=ceil(amount/50).min(2)`, stops early on a
short page, de-dupes across pages by posting id, fails open mid-loop
(page 1 still propagates its error so primary_chain can fall through to
JSearch), and re-checks cancellation between pages. JSearch maps the same
amount onto `num_pages = min(ceil(amount/10), 3)`.

The budget is driven by the requested AMOUNT, never by
BoardSearchInput::pages: the manual search path hardcodes
pages = MAX_PAGE_BUDGET and Adzuna's free tier is a daily call quota, so a
pages-driven loop would multiply the spend of every search. An amount that
fits in one page still costs exactly one request. The near-empty broaden
retry stays single-page.

Because `pages` is inert for the aggregator, the autopilot wizard now
disables the "Pages to scrape" field (with a hint, en+de) when the
aggregator is the only selected board; a mixed selection keeps it live.

The Adzuna provider moves to its own module — providers.rs crossed the R8
module-size cap.

Riders from the #884 re-verify: name commands::agent::agent_run as the
third cancel-token owner in ScraperEngine::cancel's rustdoc; scope the
cancel-idempotence test comment to idempotence; pin LocationInput's
onChange-before-onSelectSuggestion ordering at the source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: bound aggregator spend by an explicit budget, not the amount sentinel

The page loop derived its upstream budget from BoardSearchInput::amount, but
that field is sentinel-prone: autopilot_helpers sets amount = 100 to mean
"don't cap me" (it expresses its target in pages), not "fetch 100 postings".
Routing it into the loop bought 2 Adzuna calls and 3 billed JSearch pages on
every scheduled run — an hourly autopilot goes 24 to 48 calls/day against a
hard DAILY quota, and exhaustion compounds because an Adzuna error falls
through to the 3x-billed JSearch tier.

Add BoardSearchInput::provider_amount (Option<u32>, default None = cheapest
single-request form) as the only signal that buys upstream calls, and set it
solely in commands::scrape, where the amount is a count the user actually
typed. amount keeps its meaning as the output cap. SearchBudget carries the
two independently through the aggregator's orchestration.

Guarded by a differential pair of wiremock tests through search_with_providers:
an autopilot-shaped input (amount 100, no provider budget) issues exactly one
Adzuna request even when page 1 comes back full, while a manual-shaped input
pages. Verified by reintroducing the bug: the guard fails.

Also give AdzunaProvider the same base_url injection the page request has, and
cover the post-loop policy that reads the loop's post-dedup count (the
country-wide broaden retry and the guessed-market note) through search itself.

Correct three comments: the broaden retry's worst case is ADZUNA_MAX_PAGES + 1
fetches (a full page 1 that all dedupes away keeps the loop going); the
per-host limiter is nominal at this budget; and the in-loop cancellation check
is load-bearing, since without it a Stop is logged as a page failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: pin the aggregator request-to-budget mapping against mutation

The wiremock spend guards hand-construct SearchBudget, so they never observe
the request -> budget translation — rewriting it to spend `amount` kept all
126 aggregator tests green, i.e. the guards had a hole exactly on the original
bug's line.

Extract that hop into SearchBudget::from_input, now the only production
construction site (new() is #[cfg(test)]), and pin it with a pure test
asserting an autopilot-shaped input yields no provider spend while a
manual-shaped one maps its user-typed count through. Re-ran the mutation:
it now fails that test instead of passing everything.

Also correct the SearchBudget::amount docstring — the additive LinkedIn tier
is the paid opt-in one with its own spend caps (ADR-028), not "the free side"
— and the de hint, since Adzuna's free tier is quota-metered per call
(kontingentiert), not billed (abgerechnet).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: gate the paid apify tier on provider_amount and stop retrying metered 429s

The Apify LinkedIn gate read `budget.amount`, which a scheduled run passes as the
sentinel 100 — so it always opened and every autopilot run bought a full 50-item
actor run, contradicting the three doc claims that `provider_amount` is the only
thing buying upstream calls. The decision now lives in one `apify_cap` fn that
rides `provider_amount`: None means no paid run at all, Some(spend) buys only the
unmet remainder clamped to APIFY_MAX_ITEMS. Deliberate behavior change: an
Apify-enabled user's SCHEDULED runs no longer buy LinkedIn results; manual
searches, which carry a real user-typed spend target, are unchanged.

Adzuna and JSearch are metered, and fetch_text re-sends on 429/503, so the default
retries=2 made one search cost up to 9 quota calls and answered "you are over
quota" by spending more of it. Both now pin retries=0 through a shared
FetchOptions builder, mirroring the existing APIFY_RETRIES precedent so the
invariant is assertable rather than inline.

Cancellation is now a clean stop on the page-1 path too: a cancel observed
mid-flight surfaced as Err and made primary_chain log a jsearch fallback its own
cancel guard would never run, and the broaden retry could still spend one more
quota call on the way out.

Also hoists the double `req.amount.clamp(1, 100)` into one `requested_amount`.

* fix: unblock the inert autopilot page budget and announce its hint

A persisted out-of-range or non-integer `pages` still failed the wizard schema
while the aggregator-only selection had the control DISABLED — the wizard refused
to advance with no reachable way to comply. It is now normalized into the schema
range as soon as the field goes inert (the same round+clamp NumberField applies on
blur), so re-adding a pages-aware board hands back a sane, editable number.

The "why is this disabled" hint was a bare span no screen-reader user reached.
WizardField now gives its hint and error stable ids and wires them onto the
labelled control via aria-describedby, so every usage benefits.

`pagesInert` derives from the deduplicated board set rather than raw array length,
matching `aggregatorSelected` right above it.

Tests: replace the fixed 350ms sleeps in the LocationInput typeahead with
render-aware waits on a concrete suggestion, so keyboard nav can't silently pass
through the free-text fallback.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

blur), so re-adding a pages-aware board hands back a sane, editable number.

labelled control via aria-describedby, so every usage benefits.

matching `aggregatorSelected` right above it.

render-aware waits on a concrete suggestion, so keyboard nav can't silently pass
through the free-text fallback.

head_commit.message:
feat: revoke extension pairing over the bridge on token rotation (#895)

* feat: revoke extension pairing over the bridge on token rotation

Rotating the pairing token (Settings -> Regenerate, or a factory reset) left
live authenticated sockets running and the connected count up, and a
reconnecting extension only saw the deliberately silent failed-handshake close
- indistinguishable from a crashed app - so it retried the dead token forever
and never returned to its pairing view.

Adds a desktop -> extension `token.revoked` frame (TS constants + zod enum and
the Rust msg mirror, in lockstep). BridgeState::regenerate_token now signals
every live connection task, zeroes the live-connection count, then swaps the
secret, all inside the token lock so no handshake can authenticate against the
old token and miss the revoke. Only an ALREADY-AUTHENTICATED socket is sent the
frame; an unauthenticated one closes silently as before, preserving the
no-token-oracle invariant (ADR-0010). The frame carries no payload and no token
material.

The extension drops its stored token through the same local un-pair path the
popup's Unpair button uses, skips the backoff loop, and re-probes once unpaired
so the popup lands on the pairing view. Old extensions ignore an unknown wire
type, so no protocol-version bump is needed.

Also moves the msg constant table into its own module (the addition pushed
extension_bridge/mod.rs past the R8 hard LOC cap) and mentions re-pairing in the
factory-reset confirm copy (en + de).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: honor token.revoked only on an authenticated bridge session

The `handshakeFrame` intercept is a step-in-flight latch, not an auth check:
`awaitHandshakeFrame`'s `settle` nulls it the instant a step's frame is
consumed, so a frame arriving between steps - notably while `computeProof` is
awaited - fell through to the type dispatch. A port-squatter needs zero token
knowledge to send a syntactically-valid `challenge`, then a `token.revoked`, to
destroy the stored pairing credential; the revoke close path's backoff reset
made that loopable. The pre-hello window and the no-token attach (which reaches
phase `connected` with no handshake at all) were exposed the same way.

Adds a real `authenticated` flag on BridgeClient, set only where serverProof
verification completes and cleared on every attach and on close, and gates the
revoke branch on it. The branch stays below the handshake intercept so both
protections compose.

Tests: the security probe is now permanent (valid-challenge-then-revoke during
the computeProof window must not unpair), plus a stale-frame-after-close probe
and a revoke aimed at the unpaired re-probe socket - both verified to fail
without their respective guard.

Also: a failed token clear now forces bad_token instead of silently retrying a
known-dead secret, and the rotation lock-scope comments no longer overclaim
(the proof is verified outside the token lock; safety rests on
subscribe-at-accept plus the buffered broadcast).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: bind the bridge handshake verdict to the transport that earned it

WS5 defense-in-depth. `authenticated` is set after `await computeProof(...)`,
so a socket that closes inside that await had the flag cleared by `onClose` and
then set straight back by the resuming continuation - leaving it true with a
null transport until the next attach, and `setPhase('connected')` claiming a
live session over nothing. Only a valid serverProof reaches that line, so it
was not peer-reachable, but a stale-true auth flag on the bridge is worth zero
tolerance: the next frame delivered on that dead transport would be trusted.

Re-checks the captured transport identity before applying the verdict. Plain
return rather than finishHandshake: whatever ended the transport already set
its phase and armed its reconnect, and finishHandshake would null and close
`this.transport` - which in the replaced case is a different, healthy socket.

Test: socket closes during the serverProof await -> phase never becomes
connected and a following token.revoked is ignored. Verified to fail before the
guard (phase came back connected on a dead transport).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* style: apply rustfmt to extension bridge

Formatting drift from my own edits, not the main sync: the third `next_step`
argument rewrapped the read loop's match, and the new `token_revoked_reply`
assert exceeded the width. `cargo check`/`clippy`/`test` all pass on
badly-formatted code, so nothing I ran locally caught it - `cargo fmt --check`
is its own gate.

Formatting only, no behavior change: cargo test --lib extension_bridge 315
passed and clippy --all-features --all-targets is clean after the reformat.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: harden bridge pairing revocation after review

HIGH - the failed-clear branch was dead under test. Every revoke case resolved
`onTokenRevoked`, so nothing exercised the path where storage refuses to drop
the token. Covered now: rejecting the clear must surface `bad_token` and start
no re-probe, since reconnecting would put a known-dead secret back on the wire
and resume the forever-retry loop the frame exists to end.

MEDIUM - count theft. A socket parked in a long dispatch await had not polled
its revoke receiver when the rotation zeroed the count; if a browser re-paired
first, that socket's later teardown decremented a count it no longer owned and
`is_connected()` under-reported a live pairing. Adds a rotation epoch bumped
inside the same lock hold; a connection stamps the epoch it counted itself
under (read AFTER the increment) and only decrements while it still matches.

MEDIUM - the desktop no-oracle gate had no Rust coverage. Extracted as the pure
`revoke_frames(authenticated)` with both arms pinned: authenticated gets the
revoke then a close, unauthenticated gets nothing at all.

LOW - compute both handshake proofs up front, leaving zero await between
receiving `auth.ok` and setting `authenticated`; the old lazy server-proof await
sat exactly where a legitimate `token.revoked` lands and dropped it. LOW - a
closed broadcast channel is no longer treated as a revocation (it would have
mass-unpaired every browser on a channel-lifecycle change); it tears the
connection down without a frame. LOW - cancel assist streams before enqueueing
the close, so no billable chunk trails behind it. LOW - reset the revoke latches
in `attach()` like their siblings. LOW - the rotation doc now names BOTH
load-bearing invariants (single lock hold AND subscribe-at-accept).

Also splits the revoke wire surface into its own module: the epoch work pushed
extension_bridge/mod.rs past the R8 hard LOC cap again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: persist apply-by-email drafts on the generation aggregate (#894)

* feat: persist apply-by-email subject and body on the generation aggregate

The apply-by-email draft lived only in React state, so switching tabs or
restarting lost it. Persist it on the per-job aiGenerations aggregate.

Adds an additive `add_email_draft` migration (email_subject/email_body TEXT
NOT NULL DEFAULT ''), wires the two columns through AiGenerationRecord, the
row read/write paths, DataStore export/import, and the merge-upsert. The
fields merge exactly like cover_letter_text (`pick`): a regenerated or
rewritten email overwrites the stored draft, a save from another surface
leaves it untouched, and subject/body pick independently.

The tab now saves the settled stream and every accepted rewrite via
useSaveAiGeneration with the same jobUrl/board meta, so the merge-upsert
lands on the same aggregate row, and hydrates the draft from the saved
record on mount when no generation is running.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address review findings on apply-by-email draft persistence

Skip the save entirely for a URL-less Application. `ai_generations_save` keys
both the parent-Application upsert and the generation merge on the job url and
both treat '' as "no match", so every save minted a fresh `applied` Application
plus a generation row whose FK pointed at that phantom — invisible to the
FK-joined `matchingGenerations`, so hydration never fired and the draft was
still lost, now with duplicate applications. Staying session-only for those is
strictly better until the save can be keyed on applicationId.

Merge the email subject and body as ONE atomic draft rather than picking each
independently: a regeneration whose output broke the `Subject:` line contract
parsed to an empty subject and kept the PREVIOUS subject glued onto the new
body.

Blank `targetLanguage` and `mode` in the save request too, completing the
neutralisation already done for the language triad — `meta`'s fallbacks are
placeholders and clobbered stored values whenever `saved` was undefined while a
row existed.

Surface save failures: the command reports errors in-band (`{ error }`) rather
than rejecting, so nothing noticed them. Widen the save contract to the real
`{ id, success } | { error }` shape, inspect it, and warn that the draft will
not survive the tab switch.

Invalidate `applications.all` alongside `aiGenerations.all` — the save advances
the Application status server-side, which left the detail page's status chip and
timeline stale.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: recover the saved email draft when a generation fails mid-stream

A generation that threw after emitting tokens left `streamText` non-empty for
the rest of the mount, so the draft derivation never fell back to the saved
record: the persisted email stayed masked behind a half-written fragment, with
Copy and mailto acting on that fragment, until the tab was remounted. Clear the
stream on the non-abort error path and pin it with a test that rejects
mid-stream and asserts the saved draft is what is shown and copied.

Echo candidateName, jobTitle, companyName and topRequirements from the saved
record too. The doc comment already claimed the request carried nothing this
surface does not measure, but those four still fell back to profile and
Application values and clobbered stored ones through the merge whenever `saved`
was undefined while a row existed — a detach-then-re-track leaves exactly that
orphaned FK.

Model AiGenerationSaveResult as the union the command actually returns,
`{ id, success } | { error }`, so the compiler refuses a bare `.id` until the
failure arm is narrowed out. That immediately caught an unchecked read in
TailorFlow's background persist, which treated an in-band failure as success
and invalidated queries for a write that never landed.

Also: clear the stale save warning when a new generation starts, give it
role="alert" like its genError sibling rather than the weaker role="status"
that fought the ancestor aria-live region, cover the merge's mirror case
(subject without body), exercise the onError branch, and assert both
invalidations on the real useSaveAiGeneration hook.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
feat: persist apply-by-email drafts on the generation aggregate (#894)

* feat: persist apply-by-email subject and body on the generation aggregate

The apply-by-email draft lived only in React state, so switching tabs or
restarting lost it. Persist it on the per-job aiGenerations aggregate.

Adds an additive `add_email_draft` migration (email_subject/email_body TEXT
NOT NULL DEFAULT ''), wires the two columns through AiGenerationRecord, the
row read/write paths, DataStore export/import, and the merge-upsert. The
fields merge exactly like cover_letter_text (`pick`): a regenerated or
rewritten email overwrites the stored draft, a save from another surface
leaves it untouched, and subject/body pick independently.

The tab now saves the settled stream and every accepted rewrite via
useSaveAiGeneration with the same jobUrl/board meta, so the merge-upsert
lands on the same aggregate row, and hydrates the draft from the saved
record on mount when no generation is running.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: address review findings on apply-by-email draft persistence

Skip the save entirely for a URL-less Application. `ai_generations_save` keys
both the parent-Application upsert and the generation merge on the job url and
both treat '' as "no match", so every save minted a fresh `applied` Application
plus a generation row whose FK pointed at that phantom — invisible to the
FK-joined `matchingGenerations`, so hydration never fired and the draft was
still lost, now with duplicate applications. Staying session-only for those is
strictly better until the save can be keyed on applicationId.

Merge the email subject and body as ONE atomic draft rather than picking each
independently: a regeneration whose output broke the `Subject:` line contract
parsed to an empty subject and kept the PREVIOUS subject glued onto the new
body.

Blank `targetLanguage` and `mode` in the save request too, completing the
neutralisation already done for the language triad — `meta`'s fallbacks are
placeholders and clobbered stored values whenever `saved` was undefined while a
row existed.

Surface save failures: the command reports errors in-band (`{ error }`) rather
than rejecting, so nothing noticed them. Widen the save contract to the real
`{ id, success } | { error }` shape, inspect it, and warn that the draft will
not survive the tab switch.

Invalidate `applications.all` alongside `aiGenerations.all` — the save advances
the Application status server-side, which left the detail page's status chip and
timeline stale.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: recover the saved email draft when a generation fails mid-stream

A generation that threw after emitting tokens left `streamText` non-empty for
the rest of the mount, so the draft derivation never fell back to the saved
record: the persisted email stayed masked behind a half-written fragment, with
Copy and mailto acting on that fragment, until the tab was remounted. Clear the
stream on the non-abort error path and pin it with a test that rejects
mid-stream and asserts the saved draft is what is shown and copied.

Echo candidateName, jobTitle, companyName and topRequirements from the saved
record too. The doc comment already claimed the request carried nothing this
surface does not measure, but those four still fell back to profile and
Application values and clobbered stored ones through the merge whenever `saved`
was undefined while a row existed — a detach-then-re-track leaves exactly that
orphaned FK.

Model AiGenerationSaveResult as the union the command actually returns,
`{ id, success } | { error }`, so the compiler refuses a bare `.id` until the
failure arm is narrowed out. That immediately caught an unchecked read in
TailorFlow's background persist, which treated an in-band failure as success
and invalidated queries for a write that never landed.

Also: clear the stale save warning when a new generation starts, give it
role="alert" like its genError sibling rather than the weaker role="status"
that fought the ancestor aria-live region, cover the merge's mirror case
(subject without body), exercise the onError branch, and assert both
invalidations on the real useSaveAiGeneration hook.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix: interview questions review follow-ups (#891)

* fix: copy email body without subject

The Copy button under the email Body re-prepended "Subject: …" before the
body, so pasting into a mail client's body field needed a manual strip.
The subject already has its own copy button, so Copy now writes the body
only; the label becomes "Copy body" (en/de) to match.

* feat: add interview questions language selector

Output language for "questions to ask the interviewer" was implicitly the
detected meta.targetLanguage with no user control. generateInterviewQuestions
now takes an optional language CODE (resolved through OUTPUT_LANGUAGES) that
overrides the prompt's language note; market/register still derives from
meta.jobCountry so it does not drift. The hook derives a default from the ad
and persists the chosen language as the record's targetLanguage.

* feat: link prep result to its application

A completed "Prep this application" run left the user with a proposal and no
way to reach the record it wrote to. The footer now offers "View application"
on a completed run: it calls the idempotent saveFromPosting (dedupes by jobUrl,
the same key the agent's own saves used) and navigates to that application,
notifying instead when the save fails or returns no id. The proposal hint no
longer claims the run is display-only.

* fix: keep the picked question language out of shared record fields

Review follow-up. The interview-questions picker wrote its value into the
aiGenerations targetLanguage, a SHARED field the Rust merge picks non-blank-wins
and the email tab, export meta and tailor seed all read — a German job plus an
English question pick silently switched the email draft and export header. The
pick is now generation-only; the record keeps the detected language.

The hook also splits the value in two: a clamped code for the picker to display
and the raw detected language for the prompt, so an ad in a language the picker
does not offer no longer collapses to English.

The "View application" request drops jobDescription: that merge is also
non-blank-wins, so a navigation button must not overwrite a job description the
user edited on the detail page.

* fix: follow the output language in the question lexicon and picker

CI review follow-up on the interview-questions picker.

The system prompt called antiAiTellProse() with no argument, so questions
written in German were still policed by the English anti-AI-tell list; the
picked language now selects the ruleset, matching the application-answers
prompt. The prompt also names the language (getLanguageName) instead of
emitting a bare ISO code.

The picker no longer displays a clamped value while generating another
language: there is one effective language, and the ad's own language is
offered as an extra option when the list does not stock it.

The View application button closes the modal only after navigation resolves,
so a failed route no longer bins the run log. Adds the missing coverage for
generate()'s error path and for a pick surviving a jobDesc change.

* fix: clamp prompt language input and resolve names to codes

CI review follow-up.

getLanguageName returns an unrecognised string verbatim, and the result was
interpolated into the interview-questions prompt as an instruction outside the
untrusted-input fence. Since the value can originate from a scraped ad via
extractMetadata, clamp it to an ISO-639-1 shape first and drop anything else,
leaving the meta-derived note to run.

The anti-AI-tell lexicon keys off the language code, but the value can arrive
as a name, and slicing German to ge silently missed the curated German list.
toLanguageCode in shared is now the inverse of getLanguageName and normalises
once at that boundary.

All three language notes now render a language name rather than a bare code.

workflow_runs.display_title: feat: offline geonames geocoding with photon fallback (#893)

head_commit.message:
feat: offline geonames geocoding with photon fallback (#893)

* feat: offline geonames geocoding with photon fallback

Retire the public-Nominatim autocomplete: its usage policy forbids
autocomplete, and its throttling silently degraded the picker to zero
suggestions.

A bundled GeoNames index is now the primary source. The new geodata
directory under the Tauri crate carries cities15000 (34k rows, gzipped
TSV) plus countryInfo (252 rows), compiled in with include_bytes! and
include_str! — no network at build time, no new table, no new crate. The
index builds once behind a LazyLock and folds every search key through
the existing cluster normalize fold, so diacritic equivalence cannot
drift.

Ranking is exact country name, then exact city name, then prefix hits
(country prefix, city prefix, exact alternate spelling), then alternate
prefixes; population decides within a tier, so "ber" yields Berlin
rather than Bermuda and "muenchen" yields Munich.

Photon (OpenStreetMap/ODbL) is the fallback, reached only when the index
returns nothing for a query of at least three characters. A network or
parse failure degrades to no suggestions, exactly as before.

The suggest() signature and result shape are unchanged (display, lat,
lon, countryCode; capped at 5; deduped), so geocode_suggest,
LocationInput and the autopilot country-code backfill need no changes.

GeoNames is CC BY 4.0 and Photon serves ODbL data, so attribution ships
in Settings, About (en and de) and in the geodata README, ADR-0005 and
the scraping knowledge doc. Regenerate the assets with pnpm gen:geonames.

* fix: resolve country codes and endonyms exactly in offline geocoding

Country rows were indexed by English name only, so a typed country code or
endonym prefix-matched an unrelated city and returned five confident-looking
rows: usa/us gave Uşak (TR), uk gave Ukraine, de gave DR Congo, gb gave Gboko
(NG), schweiz gave Schweizer-Reneke (ZA). Callers take the first suggestion's
country code, so entering "Schweiz" persisted za — a live Adzuna market, i.e. a
silent switch to South African jobs.

Three changes close it. countries.tsv now carries ISO3 (countryInfo column 1),
and both ISO codes are matched exact-only, never as a prefix. A small curated
endonym table (deutschland, schweiz, suisse, uk, espana, …) lives in Rust rather
than the asset, so regenerating from upstream cannot wipe it. And the online
fallback is gated on match quality instead of non-emptiness: the index now
reports whether anything matched a key exactly, and an inexact result no longer
vetoes the Photon lookup that would have answered correctly. Inexact hits use a
higher query-length floor than misses do, so partial typing ("ber", "berli")
still stays offline.

The picker's own "City, Country" label is retried against the text before the
first comma, so re-opening the dropdown resolves offline instead of always
going online.

The UI package no longer ships a geocoder: onFetchSuggestions is required on
both useGeocoding and LocationInput, and the Nominatim defaultFetch is deleted.
It was reachable — the published Storybook rendered LocationInput without the
prop, issuing live browser-side autocomplete traffic with no user agent.

Also: cap the query length before building a third-party URL, correct the
index-cost comments with measured numbers, drop the postcode claim from the
story placeholder, and pin all of the above with tests, including the Photon
request shape, user agent and timeout against a local mock server.

* fix: make the geocoding fallback and index degradation testable

The Photon branch of suggest() could not be reached from a test: photon()
hardcoded the endpoint, so every suggest() test returned at the offline
early-return and the merge rule — Photon replaces a weak offline hit, an
empty or failed Photon answer leaves the offline rows alone — was asserted
nowhere. A suggest_at(endpoint, query) seam mirrors the existing photon_at
one, and three mock-server tests now pin each branch. The tests that rely on
an offline early-return also assert the query really is an exact index hit,
so asset drift fails them instead of quietly making CI issue live requests.

Index construction gets the same treatment: parse() and decode_cities() are
split out of load(), and their degradation arms are covered — corrupt gzip,
short and long rows, non-numeric coordinates, empty names, malformed country
codes, unparseable population, a duplicate country code, and an alias whose
country is absent from the asset.

Confidence is now read only from the rows that survive into the returned
suggestions. An exact hit ranked below the cap is invisible to the caller,
so letting it set the flag vetoed the fallback on the strength of a row
nobody was shown.

Also in this round: the index is warmed from setup on a blocking thread,
since derive_country_code's timeout cannot interrupt a synchronous build;
queries in scripts the asset cannot hold skip the length floors instead of
being permanently unanswerable; the last 32 lookups are memoized, and only
when non-empty so a transient failure is retried; country codes are checked
for ASCII letters rather than byte length; both assets carry a recorded
SHA-256 and fetch date that a test asserts; the egress ADR states the
exemption that makes a user-typed lookup different from enrichment; and the
attribution line is legible enough for a credit we are required to show.

* test: supply the required geocoder stub in the drawer escape test

The drawer's Escape-layering test renders LocationInput, whose
onFetchSuggestions prop became required on this branch so the component can
never fall back to live third-party autocomplete. The case only cares about
Escape reaching the right layer, so an empty result set is enough.

suggestions.

A bundled GeoNames index is now the primary source. The new geodata
directory under the Tauri crate carries cities15000 (34k rows, gzipped
TSV) plus countryInfo (252 rows), compiled in with include_bytes! and
include_str! — no network at build time, no new table, no new crate. The
index builds once behind a LazyLock and folds every search key through
the existing cluster normalize fold, so diacritic equivalence cannot
drift.

Ranking is exact country name, then exact city name, then prefix hits
(country prefix, city prefix, exact alternate spelling), then alternate
prefixes; population decides within a tier, so "ber" yields Berlin
rather than Bermuda and "muenchen" yields Munich.

Photon (OpenStreetMap/ODbL) is the fallback, reached only when the index
returns nothing for a query of at least three characters. A network or
parse failure degrades to no suggestions, exactly as before.

The suggest() signature and result shape are unchanged (display, lat,
lon, countryCode; capped at 5; deduped), so geocode_suggest,
LocationInput and the autopilot country-code backfill need no changes.

GeoNames is CC BY 4.0 and Photon serves ODbL data, so attribution ships
in Settings, About (en and de) and in the geodata README, ADR-0005 and
the scraping knowledge doc. Regenerate the assets with pnpm gen:geonames.

* fix: resolve country codes and endonyms exactly in offline geocoding

Country rows were indexed by English name only, so a typed country code or
endonym prefix-matched an unrelated city and returned five confident-looking
rows: usa/us gave Uşak (TR), uk gave Ukraine, de gave DR Congo, gb gave Gboko
(NG), schweiz gave Schweizer-Reneke (ZA). Callers take the first suggestion's
country code, so entering "Schweiz" persisted za — a live Adzuna market, i.e. a
silent switch to South African jobs.

and both ISO codes are matched exact-only, never as a prefix. A small curated
endonym table (deutschland, schweiz, suisse, uk, espana, …) lives in Rust rather
than the asset, so regenerating from upstream cannot wipe it. And the online
fallback is gated on match quality instead of non-emptiness: the index now
reports whether anything matched a key exactly, and an inexact result no longer
vetoes the Photon lookup that would have answered correctly. Inexact hits use a
higher query-length floor than misses do, so partial typing ("ber", "berli")
still stays offline.

first comma, so re-opening the dropdown resolves offline instead of always
going online.

The UI package no longer ships a geocoder: onFetchSuggestions is required on
both useGeocoding and LocationInput, and the Nominatim defaultFetch is deleted.
It was reachable — the published Storybook rendered LocationInput without the
prop, issuing live browser-side autocomplete traffic with no user agent.

index-cost comments with measured numbers, drop the postcode claim from the
story placeholder, and pin all of the above with tests, including the Photon
request shape, user agent and timeout against a local mock server.

* fix: make the geocoding fallback and index degradation testable

The Photon branch of suggest() could not be reached from a test: photon()
hardcoded the endpoint, so every suggest() test returned at the offline
early-return and the merge rule — Photon replaces a weak offline hit, an
empty or failed Photon answer leaves the offline rows alone — was asserted
nowhere. A suggest_at(endpoint, query) seam mirrors the existing photon_at
one, and three mock-server tests now pin each branch. The tests that rely on
an offline early-return also assert the query really is an exact index hit,
so asset drift fails them instead of quietly making CI issue live requests.

Index construction gets the same treatment: parse() and decode_cities() are
split out of load(), and their degradation arms are covered — corrupt gzip,
short and long rows, non-numeric coordinates, empty names, malformed country
codes, unparseable population, a duplicate country code, and an alias whose
country is absent from the asset.

Confidence is now read only from the rows that survive into the returned
suggestions. An exact hit ranked below the cap is invisible to the caller,
so letting it set the flag vetoed the fallback on the strength of a row
nobody was shown.

Also in this round: the index is warmed from setup on a blocking thread,
since derive_country_code's timeout cannot interrupt a synchronous build;
queries in scripts the asset cannot hold skip the length floors instead of
being permanently unanswerable; the last 32 lookups are memoized, and only
when non-empty so a transient failure is retried; country codes are checked
for ASCII letters rather than byte length; both assets carry a recorded
SHA-256 and fetch date that a test asserts; the egress ADR states the
exemption that makes a user-typed lookup different from enrichment; and the
attribution line is legible enough for a credit we are required to show.

* test: supply the required geocoder stub in the drawer escape test

The drawer's Escape-layering test renders LocationInput, whose
onFetchSuggestions prop became required on this branch so the component can
never fall back to live third-party autocomplete. The case only cares about
Escape reaching the right layer, so an empty result set is enough.

head_commit.message:
feat: jobs page command bar, scrape drawer, responsive split view (#892)

* feat: add a right slide-over drawer primitive to the ui package

Drawer is the lateral sibling of ModalShell: same portal + scrim + focus
trap + Escape contract, but pinned full-height to the right edge. Use it
for a task surface the user edits then applies (a filter/search form),
where the content behind should stay legible.

- variants.slideOverRight: full-width horizontal travel for a sheet.
  Under prefers-reduced-motion the translate is dropped entirely (opacity
  only) rather than shortened, so there is no positional jump.
- Focus returns to the control that opened the drawer on close
  (WCAG 2.4.3); the capture effect is declared before useFocusTrap so it
  still sees the opener as activeElement.
- Tag gains an optional closeLabel so several closable tags in a row do
  not all announce as an identical "Close" (mirrors CompanyTypeahead's
  per-chip removeLabel). Defaults to the previous literal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: move the jobs scrape form into a slide-over drawer behind a command bar

Replaces the Jobs hero (big title + subtitle + eyebrow + inline scrape
form) with one compact JobsCommandBar and a right slide-over drawer.

Command bar: title, filter input, sort, hide-agency toggle, shown/total
count, list/split toggle, Clear and Scrape. The row is flex-wrap with no
no-wrap shrink-0 container, so at the 900x600 window floor the trailing
action group wraps to a second line instead of being clipped — the old
PageHeader actions slot pinned it at max-content. PageHeader itself is
untouched, so its other four consumers are unaffected.

A second thin row appears only when it has content: removable chips for
the active text filter and hide-agency (per-chip x plus clear-all),
followed by the existing BoardSummaryChips and the sanitized last-scrape
failure note. A third row carries the live scrape label and Cancel —
with the form now in a drawer that auto-closes as results stream in,
that is the only remaining cancel affordance.

The drawer reuses ScrapeForm and ScrapeFilters verbatim; batch-apply is
unchanged (edits take effect on Search). Its body owns the scroll, which
replaces the bounded max-h-[55vh] overflow-y-auto page wrapper — that
wrapper is what produced the stray horizontal scrollbar, and removing it
also hands the results area the full remaining height.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: jobs split view responsive widths and detail action wrap

md: is always active at the 900x600 window floor (PATTERNS §15), so the
fixed md:w-[420px] xl:w-[480px] 2xl:w-[520px] ladder left the detail pane
about 248px at the floor. The list pane is now proportional with a floor
and a ceiling — md:w-[34%] md:min-w-[280px] md:max-w-[480px] md:shrink-0
— which keeps the detail pane usable at every supported width.

The split root also gains w-full min-w-0: as the lone flex child of the
results card its main size resolved to max-content, so the two panes
overflowed the card and were clipped by its overflow-hidden.

The detail header action cluster was shrink-0 flex-wrap, which pins it at
max-content so the wrap never fired and Tailor/Prep/... were clipped by
four overflow-hidden ancestors. Dropping shrink-0 and adding min-w-0 lets
it shrink below max-content so the wrap happens. The header is now an
@container and the cluster takes a full-width row under a ~672px pane,
returning inline and right-aligned above it — a panel-width decision, so
a container query rather than a viewport breakpoint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: harden the jobs drawer and command bar against the ui-ux audit findings

Shared-primitive half of the review round.

Drawer
- Lift ModalShell's ref-counted `.modal-blur-active` body class into
  lib/modal-blur and call it from both. A portaled overlay's own
  backdrop-filter does not composite under WebView2, so without it the
  drawer's glass degrades to a flat scrim on the shipping platform.
- `returnFocusTo`: where focus goes on close when the control that opened
  the drawer is gone — the empty-state CTA is replaced by the drawer's own
  action, so focus was landing on <body> (WCAG 2.4.3). `<body>` is also
  rejected as a target, since that is what activeElement degrades to when
  the focused node is removed.
- Export drawerVariants/drawerTransition as pure functions of the motion
  preference, so the reduced-motion branch is unit-testable without
  driving matchMedia through a tree. Slide is now `relaxed` (220ms), not
  `normal` (180ms): a full panel width in 180ms reads as a snap.

Escape layering
- An OPEN Dropdown/CompanyTypeahead popover now consumes Escape instead of
  letting it reach an ancestor dialog and close the whole surface. React
  delegates from the root container, below `window`, so stopping there is
  enough; a CLOSED popover still lets Escape through, as it should.

Other
- Dropdown takes `aria-label` — its trigger's only accessible name was the
  selected option ("Newest first"), which never mentions sorting.
- Tag's close button gets `-m-1 p-1`: a ~24px hit box (WCAG 2.5.8) around
  the 11px glyph, with no layout change.
- en: sentence-case "Scrape jobs". de: narrow no-break space (U+202F)
  before the percent sign. Drop the now-unused filters.clearAll.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: close the jobs scrape drawer on submit and shrink the command bar

Renderer half of the review round; measured in headless Chromium against
the built stylesheet at 900x600 with the sidebar expanded (496px content
column) in German, the worst case.

Focus (WCAG 2.4.3). The drawer used to close from an effect on
livePostings.length — a BACKGROUND stream event. That yanked focus out
from under whatever the user was doing, and on the first-run path
(empty state -> "Search jobs" -> drawer) the CTA the drawer would return
focus to had already unmounted, dropping focus to <body>. It now closes
in the user-initiated submit handler, and the page hands the drawer the
always-mounted Scrape button as a focus-return fallback. The same change
fixes a scrape that returns ZERO results leaving the drawer stranded
open, since nothing ever streamed.

Contrast. The status strip was text-foreground/55; the light-legibility
remap in utilities.css lifts only /20…/50, so /55 renders LIGHTER than
/50 — measured 3.81:1 on the one row carrying the only Cancel control.
Now /70: 6.15:1 light, 8.47:1 dark.

Height at the floor. Bar 306px -> 236px (51% -> 39% of the window), so
the results list grows 294px -> 364px. Drivers removed: the hide-agency
chip (its toggle is already visible 40px above), the clear-all beside a
single removable chip, and a wrapping diagnostics row — the chips row is
now strictly one line that scrolls sideways (98px -> 28px).

Drawer content. ScrapeForm becomes the drawer's pinned-chrome panel:
shrink-0 header, ONE scrolling body, shrink-0 footer. Its content
overflows at this size (550px in a 477px body), and Start used to scroll
below the fold; it is now always visible. Dropping the nested GlassCard
also removes a surface-in-surface frame and the doubled entrance
animation (drawer slide + card fade), whose raw inline transition
ignored prefers-reduced-motion.

Split gate. `md:` is a VIEWPORT breakpoint and always matched at the
900px floor, so a 416px card still tried to seat two panes: the list took
all 409px and the detail pane measured 0px — the job was invisible. The
results card is now an @container and the split gates on `@3xl`, giving
one 409px pane with a Back button instead.

Also: h1 off the gradient onto the text-body-strong precedent; the count
moves beside the input it describes and drops its prohibited span
aria-label for a real sr-only string; the remove-filter label carries the
bare query (no double colon); the status strip reuses the results
skeleton's scanning copy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make the jobs chips row keyboard-reachable and widen the split gate

Closes the UX critic's final round (WS9).

Chips row keyboard access. The row scrolls horizontally (scrollWidth 977 vs
clientWidth 520), so everything past its right edge was unreachable: only
the leftmost chip's close button was a tab stop, and that single focusable
descendant is exactly what keeps axe's scrollable-region-focusable rule
quiet. The container now carries tabIndex={0} plus the group role and
label, and an explicit focus-visible ring — a focusable div renders none by
default. The inner wrapper that previously held the group role is gone, so
the label is not duplicated on a nested node.

Split gate 48rem -> 42rem. The rem root is 17px (utilities.css: the Apple
body baseline), so @3xl meant 816px of card width and @2xl means 714px —
two-pane now arrives ~100px of card width sooner. Swept against the built
stylesheet in headless Chromium with the sidebar expanded: the flip lands
at a 1225px window (card 736px) and yields 280px of list + 454px of
detail, both above the 280px floor. Narrow-window usability was the
original complaint, so the earlier flip is the point.

Tag close target. p-1 measured 19.5px, not the ~24px the comment claimed.
p-1.5 takes the 11px glyph to ~23.5px (WCAG 2.5.8); the negative margins
grow with it so nothing shifts.

Progress stutter. The label under the results ProgressBar rendered the
SAME copy as the command bar's status strip ~60px above, updating out of
step. The label is gone; the fill stays, and the strip remains the labelled
surface (it also owns Cancel).

Not touched, noted for a separate primitives sweep: CheckableTag checked
3.05:1, ghost Button 3.94:1 and processing Tag 4.48:1 on light are shared
@ajh/ui contrast debt, not introduced here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop location suggestions closing the scrape drawer on escape

Closes the #892 CI review.

HIGH — the Escape-layering contract had a third call site I missed.
LocationInput closed its suggestion panel without stopPropagation, and it
reaches the drawer through ScrapeFilters, so dismissing suggestions tore
the whole drawer down. Same bug class already fixed for Dropdown and
CompanyTypeahead; mirrored their guard. Verified the new
LocationInput-in-drawer test FAILS without it (onClose called once on the
first Escape) rather than trusting it green. useDropdownKeyboard now
carries the contract comment naming every implementor; ActionMenu is
called out as the next candidate but left alone — its Escape handler is a
document listener, so the fix there differs.

MEDIUM — the chips row announced "Active filters" even when it held only
scrape diagnostics and no filter. The label now follows the contents:
filters.activeLabel with a filter applied, a neutral commandBar.statusRow
key otherwise (en+de).

MEDIUM — live regions were mounted together with their text, which NVDA
and JAWS announce unreliably: the region has to pre-exist so the CHANGE is
what fires. This one matters because the strip is the sole Cancel
affordance once the drawer closes. The bar now keeps one always-mounted
empty sr-only role=status and writes scanning progress or the failure note
into it; the visual copies are aria-hidden so nothing is announced twice.
Cancel stays exposed — it is a control, not status.

LOW — corrected the @2xl threshold comment in JobDetailPane. The container
is the header, so 42rem is measured against its CONTENT box; measured in
headless Chromium, that is 714px at the app's 17px rem root, i.e. a ~757px
pane, not the ~672px the comment claimed.

LOW — the filter input's aria-label was its placeholder, which is an
instruction and reads as one in the rotor; added a short
commandBar.filterLabel (en+de).

Also made the layout-contract test anchor on the title instead of
firstElementChild (the new live region is now first) and match class
tokens rather than substrings.

Keyboard or trackpad reports hover:hover + pointer:fine, so a coarse gate
skipped priming there while WebKit still gated media loading on a gesture —
posters forever on exactly that configuration. maxTouchPoints covers every
touch-capable browser; a Windows touch laptop just takes a harmless muted
play/pause and a real desktop reports 0 and never primes. `coarse` still
gates the particle drop and the URL-bar resize guard.

The video error handler now starts with an identity guard. Media elements can
error more than once and a discarded element outlives its replacement, so a
late error was resetting the segment while the live clip was still mounted —
freezing it and stacking a second video into the scene on the next tick. The
teardown also revokes the discarded blob URL; live clips keep theirs by
design, but a failing segment was leaking one multi-MB blob per retry.
play() returning a non-promise now pauses immediately instead of leaving the
clip running under the scrubber.

Tests go 12 to 16: a non-touch desktop never-prime lock, a trackpad-iPad
priming case, the non-promise pause, and the stale-error clobber. ADR-0019's
deviation log records the canTouch rationale, the identity guard and revoke,
and names eps as the third consumer of the frozen isMobile.

* fix: guard every world clip listener against a replaced element

Applies the PR #890 CI review advisories on the /world engine.

The identity guard added for the error listener covered only that listener.
A media element keeps firing after the segment has torn it down and replaced
it, so a late loadedmetadata from a discarded video set s.ready while the live
clip had no metadata at all, and raf() then scrubbed it against the
duration || 1 fallback; a late seeked hid the poster to reveal a video that
was never painted. All the listeners now share one liveness check.

Teardown clears the source and re-runs the load algorithm before revoking the
blob URL — a detached element can hold decoder resources until its source is
dropped, and the retry path makes up to three per segment. Priming gains a
primeTries cap mirroring tries, since a refusal deliberately clears primed and
a browser refusing muted playback outright would otherwise take a fresh play()
on every pointerdown for the life of the page.

The header MOBILE block no longer lists the particle drop and the URL-bar
resize guard as phone-tier behaviour: both key off the coarse pointer alone
and apply to tablets, which contradicted the inline comments and the ADR.

Adds the eps test, the one frozen-isMobile consumer no assertion could see
because every test stubs rAF away: one hand-rolled frame at a scroll offset
where the lerped step falls between the two seek thresholds, so a tablet
mount seeks and a phone mount coalesces. Also covers the late-loadedmetadata
guard and the prime cap, and documents the test file's cross-mount coupling.

* fix: return a disposer from the world engine mount

Applies the CodeRabbit review on PR #890.

mountScrollWorld returned nothing and never unregistered: six window
listeners, a self-rescheduling rAF loop and every clip's blob URL outlived
the mount, so StrictMode's dev double-invoke or a client-side route change
stacked a whole second engine over the first, driving detached DOM forever.
It now returns an idempotent disposer that cancels the pending frame, removes
the listeners, releases each clip and empties the container; read() and raf()
early-return once torn down, and a clip whose fetch resolves after teardown is
dropped instead of appended to a dead scene. An empty config returns a no-op
disposer rather than undefined. The injected style element stays: it is
id-guarded and may be shared with another live mount.

WorldClient returns the disposer straight from its effect and drops the
mountedRef latch that only existed because teardown was impossible, so /world
no longer has to be entered via a full navigation. scrub-engine.d.ts carries
the new return type.

Clip release is now one shared helper used by both the error path and the
disposer, and it pauses before clearing the source so a detached element
cannot sit on decoder resources.

Tests: dispose every mount in afterEach rather than relying only on per-mount
asset-path scoping, restore the stubbed screen dimensions, cover the classifier
threshold from both sides, and add teardown coverage.

The ADR deviation log gains D6 for the disposer and swaps the copied
thresholds in D2 to D4 for pointers at the symbols that own them.
